item.evidence: backend/server.py:356-358 and :386-388 default all headers to None; :378 checks `model not in ALLOWED_MODELS.get(provider or "", [])` and :379 returns 400. There is no normalization to the default provider/model before run_job at :367.
item.expected: R-133: "with no provider or model ... use Google Gemini with gemini-3.5-flash-lite". The OpenAPI contract also marks both headers optional. A key-only caller should reach the free default model.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: a signed-in caller sending a valid Gemini key and prompt but omitting the optional provider/model headers is rejected before a job starts. The UI sends both headers and remains usable; API users must discover and supply undocumented defaults themselves. Source prediction, not an executed request.
reproduction_steps: Sign in and POST /api/generate with a valid prompt and X-LLM-Key only.
The server returns 400 'Pick a supported provider and model' instead of starting the default Gemini job.
POST /api/ai/test-key with only X-LLM-Key has the same result.
item.title: API callers cannot synthesize with only their Gemini key — optional provider/model headers have no defaults

item.evidence: backend/projects.py:198-200 queries snapshots newest-first then calls `.to_list(200)` with no cursor or paging; frontend/src/pages/Workspace.jsx:388 uses exactly that list and :408-412 builds all selector options from it.
item.expected: request: "Keep every saved version of a project so Compare works against any earlier one, not just the last"; R-130: "lists every snapshot"; R-131: "every saved version of the open project". All saved versions must be reachable, with pagination if necessary.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: after 201 saves, v1 still exists but is absent from the history response and Compare selector; subsequent saves hide more old versions. Team members cannot use the UI to compare those earlier systems. Recent comparisons remain available. Source-backed prediction.
reproduction_steps: Create a project and save it until it has 201 versions.
Reopen it, choose Compare and open Compare against.
Observe that only v201 through v2 are offered, with no way to reach v1.
item.title: Long-lived projects lose access to older Compare versions — history silently stops at 200 saves

item.evidence: backend/projects.py:179-181 overwrites the existing project system before :190 snapshots only `res` (the new version). Snapshots are otherwise created only by new-project create at :143. backend/server.py:59-71 startup creates indexes and seeds admin/storage but performs no version backfill; versions reads at projects.py:198 and :208 read only project_versions.
item.expected: request: "Keep every saved version of a project so Compare works against any earlier one"; checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: "Trace writes ... and later reads". At minimum the saved version present when enabling history must be retained before the next overwrite; already-overwritten pre-feature versions are not assumed recoverable.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: a project saved before this update has no snapshot row. Its first post-update save replaces its old system and records only the new system. The previously saved system then cannot be retrieved or selected in Compare, even though it was present when history was introduced. This is a source prediction for existing installations; no historical database was inspected.
reproduction_steps: Use a project that existed before version history was added.
Open Compare: its existing saved version is absent.
Regenerate and Save, then reopen Compare.
Only the new version is present; the saved system that existed before this save has been overwritten without a snapshot.
item.title: Existing projects cannot compare their pre-update saved version — history has no backfill before overwrite

item.evidence: AiKeyModal.jsx:71-72 unconditionally calls `setTest(data)` when a request finishes; :81-84, :87-89, :92-97 and :140 change inputs/reset test without canceling earlier requests; :107-108 trusts any existing test result when saving a paid model. The Save button at :172 has no pending disabled condition.
item.expected: R-127: "checks the currently pasted key and model"; R-136 requires the error to apply to the selected model. Checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: "Resolve ... pending, success, failure ... against the actual operation state." Results and Save guards must match the exact key/provider/model tested.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: start a test for key A, replace it with key B, then let A's response arrive. The modal reports A's success/failure beside B and Save uses that stale result. Likewise switching from Pro to Flash-Lite during a pending Pro test can later show a paid-key error for Flash-Lite. Users can be falsely told a replacement key works or be blocked by a failure unrelated to their current selection. They can recover by retesting after all requests settle. Source prediction.
reproduction_steps: Paste key A and click Test key.
Before it finishes, replace it with key B (or change the model).
Let A's response finish.
The modal shows A's result next to the new configuration; saving a paid model consumes that result without testing the new configuration.
item.surface: AI key modal → Test key, model/provider selector, Save key
item.title: Key settings can display or enforce a result for a different key/model — asynchronous tests are not tied to the tested configuration

item.evidence: backend/server.py:280-281 maps OpenAI `insufficient_quota` to paid_model_required. Workspace.jsx:636 constructs `{ ...aiKey, provider: "gemini", model: DEFAULT_MODEL }` and persists it without replacing the key. AiKeyModal.jsx:87-90 likewise changes provider/model only.
item.expected: R-138 requires a recovery that updates the saved model/key configuration to the free model; request: "suggest switching back to Gemini Flash-Lite". Checklist, Third-party integrations: "Trace ... configuration ... request construction ... delivered outcome." A provider switch must request a compatible key instead of presenting an incompatible saved credential as ready.
item.observed: Third-party integrations: an OpenAI user with exhausted credits receives the suggested Gemini recovery. Clicking it keeps their OpenAI credential but sends it to Google on the next synthesis; the app announces a successful switch although the key cannot authenticate to the new provider. Generation still fails until the user independently obtains and enters a Gemini key. Source prediction.
reproduction_steps: Save an OpenAI key whose provider returns insufficient_quota.
Attempt Synthesize, then press Switch to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite in the error banner.
Synthesize again: the OpenAI key is now sent as the Gemini credential and fails.
The same incompatible-key retention occurs with Switch to free in settings.
item.surface: Synthesis Failed banner and AI key modal → Switch to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite
item.title: OpenAI quota recovery saves an unusable Gemini configuration — Switch to free keeps the OpenAI key

item.evidence: SystemOutput at server.py:142-154 gives strings no min_length and lists no min_length. At :340-344 parsed JSON is passed directly into that model; :349 marks it done with the model dump. Workspace.jsx:213-217 replaces the current output and announces success for any done result.
item.expected: R-143: "a provider reply that is empty, not parsable or missing the system sections fails the job instead of producing a blank or partial system"; R-105 says "renders no placeholder or empty system". Required sections must have usable content before the job is marked done.
item.observed: AI and model features: a provider JSON reply containing every required field but empty code/pseudocode strings and empty graph/setup/parameter/module arrays passes validation. The user sees a successful generation with blank tabs; on regeneration this replaces their useful current result and can be saved over the project. The old cloud version can be reopened if one exists, or the user can retry. This is a concrete accepted provider-output condition, not a claim that a live model returned it.
reproduction_steps: Start a generate or regenerate with a valid key.
Condition: provider returns valid JSON with the required field names but empty strings for code/pseudocode and empty arrays for graph/setup/parameters/modules.
The job reports done and the workspace replaces the result with blank content instead of displaying an incomplete-output failure.
item.title: Empty generated systems are accepted as finished — output validation checks types but not required content

item.evidence: Workspace.jsx:263 sends stacked systems through compactForApi, which at changes.js:75-83 omits cpp_source, pseudocode, graph and setup and slices the header to 2500 chars. server.py:248 reduces that header again to 1800. For regeneration :227 and :230-231 slice header/source to 8000 chars and pseudocode to 6000 even when full=True.
item.expected: request: "Stack Systems ... keep working with cloud projects" and "combine ... saved systems"; R-129 requires a merged system and updated regeneration; checklist, AI and model features: "transformations, truncation ... could remove essential meaning". Code that is to be preserved or merged must reach the model, or truncation must be disclosed/rejected.
item.observed: AI and model features: stack two saved components with custom behavior only in their cpp_source: none of that implementation reaches Gemini/OpenAI. Regenerate a saved header/source longer than 8000 characters: trailing functions never reach the revision prompt. The model is instructed to preserve/merge work it cannot see, so exact preservation of that behavior is unsupported and users risk losing it in a saved result. This proves omitted grounding, not a measured model response; users can manually reattach code as a workaround.
reproduction_steps: Save two generated systems containing distinct custom function bodies in cpp_source.
Select both in Projects and press Stack 2 systems.
The provider receives only summaries, parameters/modules and truncated headers, not either implementation.
Alternatively regenerate a project with code beyond the 8000-character cutoff; the trailing implementation is absent from the revision context.
item.title: Synthesis omits existing implementation during stack and long regenerations — context compaction silently drops code
